Routing observations:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected on 9 of 10 attempts.
- The only accepted C case was REQ-2408: small shipment, north region, from Regional Ops, second attempt/previous form bounced.
- Do not select C merely because the request mentions a regional office or regional origin; similar east/south cases were rejected.
- Large requests may plausibly require B (priority desk), but this is not directly confirmed by any accepted example.
- Small requests may plausibly require A (standard queue), but this is also unconfirmed.
- The available evidence is insufficient to establish a complete routing rule. Prefer A/B over C unless the case closely matches the accepted north-region, small-shipment, Regional Ops pattern.

Routing observations:
- Option C (“regional office”) remains rarely accepted: only confirmed success is REQ-2408, a small north-region shipment from Regional Ops, on a second attempt after the first form bounced.
- Do not choose C solely because a request mentions a regional office or regional origin; comparable east/south cases were rejected or have no C evidence.
- A is now confirmed for some small requests: REQ-2410 (small east claim, Regional Ops), REQ-2418 (small south claim, Regional Ops), and REQ-2419 (small south shipment, Regional Ops, second attempt).
- Small size alone does not justify A: REQ-2417 (small east shipment, Client Services) was rejected with A.
- A was rejected for large north invoice and large south shipment cases.
- B was rejected for all tested large cases (north shipment; east claim and invoices), so “large = priority desk” is contradicted by current evidence.
- The successful cases suggest source/department, request type, region, and possibly prior-attempt context matter; no complete routing rule is established.
- Prefer A for small requests when the case resembles the accepted Regional Ops examples, but remain cautious for non-Regional-Ops or east-region shipments. Avoid B absent stronger evidence; use C only for a close match to the known accepted C pattern.

Routing observations:
- No complete routing rule is established; source/department, request type, region, size, urgency/prior attempts, and possibly form details all matter.
- A has mixed results for small Regional Ops requests: accepted REQ-2410 (east claim), REQ-2418 (south claim), REQ-2419 (south shipment), and REQ-2421 (east refund); rejected REQ-2420 (north claim), REQ-2427 (east invoice with repeated client follow-up), and REQ-2428 (east shipment, second attempt). Thus do not assume small or Regional Ops implies A.
- A was also rejected for small east shipment from Client Services (REQ-2417) and large north/south cases.
- C remains rarely accepted: only confirmed success is REQ-2408, a small north shipment from Regional Ops on a second attempt after the first form bounced. Do not select C solely from regional wording; east second-attempt shipment REQ-2428 rejected A but provides no confirmed C result.
- B has no confirmed successes and was rejected in all tested large cases; “large = priority desk” remains unsupported.
- D is newly confirmed for Partner Accounts: accepted REQ-2423 (small east invoice) and REQ-2429 (large north claim). However, D was rejected as invalid in several other attempts (REQ-2422, 2424–2426), so use only for close Partner Accounts-like matches and verify that D is an available option.
- Prefer evidence-matched routing over size/region heuristics. Treat department and request type as especially important; prior-attempt context is suggestive but not decisive.

Routing observations:
- No complete routing rule is established. Department/source and request type appear especially important; region, size, urgency, prior attempts, and wording/form details may also matter.
- A is not a general default. Confirmed successes include Regional Ops small south claim (REQ-2433, REQ-2439), Regional Ops small south invoice (REQ-2438), Finance Desk large south invoice (REQ-2435), plus earlier Regional Ops small east/south claims, shipment, and refund. A was rejected for Field Sales large north/east invoices (REQ-2430, REQ-2437), Client Services small north invoice (REQ-2434), and several other mismatched cases.
- C remains rarely accepted: only confirmed success is REQ-2408, a small north shipment from Regional Ops on a second attempt after the first form bounced. C was invalid for Finance Desk large north claim (REQ-2432); do not infer C from region, size, or prior attempts.
- B still has no confirmed successes and was rejected in tested large cases. “Large = priority desk” remains unsupported.
- D is not broadly valid even for Partner Accounts. Earlier successes were Partner Accounts small east invoice (REQ-2423) and large north claim (REQ-2429), but D was invalid for Partner Accounts small east shipment (REQ-2431) and small north refund (REQ-2436), as well as several earlier attempts. Use D only for close, request-type-specific Partner Accounts matches and verify it is available.
- Department/request-type combinations likely define routing more than size or region: Finance large south invoice accepted while Finance large north claim rejected C; Regional Ops small south invoice/claim consistently accepted A.
- Prefer the closest confirmed department + request-type match; do not rely on urgency wording or “regional office” phrasing alone.

Routing observations:
- No complete routing rule is established. Department/source and request type remain most informative; region, size, urgency, wording, and prior attempts may modify routing but are not reliable alone.
- A is not a general default. Confirmed successes now include Finance Desk large north shipment (REQ-2444), Finance Desk large south invoice (REQ-2435, REQ-2449), Field Sales large south claim (REQ-2445), Regional Ops small south claim/invoice (REQ-2433, REQ-2439, REQ-2438), and earlier Regional Ops small east/south claims. A was rejected for Client Services small east shipment (REQ-2440), Finance Desk large east shipment (REQ-2441), Regional Ops small east shipment (REQ-2446), Field Sales large north/east invoices (REQ-2430, REQ-2437, REQ-2442), Client Services small north invoice (REQ-2434), and other mismatches.
- C remains rarely accepted: only confirmed success is REQ-2408, a small north shipment from Regional Ops on a second attempt after the first form bounced. C was invalid for Finance Desk large north claim (REQ-2432); do not infer C from region, size, or prior attempts.
- B still has no confirmed successes and was rejected in tested large cases, including Field Sales large east invoice (REQ-2442). “Large = priority desk” remains unsupported.
- D is not broadly valid, including for Partner Accounts. Confirmed successes are Partner Accounts small east invoice (REQ-2423) and large north claim (REQ-2429). D was rejected for Partner Accounts small east shipment (REQ-2431), small north refund (REQ-2436), small south shipment (REQ-2443), large east invoice (REQ-2447), and small south invoice (REQ-2448).
- Prefer the closest confirmed department + request-type match; do not rely on urgency or “regional office” wording alone. Verify option availability and expect exceptions even within a department.

Routing observations:
- No complete rule is established. Department/source and request type are most informative; region, size, urgency, wording, and prior attempts are unreliable alone.
- A is not a general default, but is repeatedly valid for Field Sales large claims (north/east/south: REQ-2450, REQ-2455, REQ-2459; also REQ-2445), Regional Ops small claims (including south REQ-2452), and some Finance Desk large north/south cases. It was rejected for Finance Desk large east invoice/refund (REQ-2441, REQ-2451, REQ-2457), Regional Ops small east shipment/refund and north refund (REQ-2446, REQ-2454, REQ-2456), Field Sales large north/east invoices, Client Services cases, and other mismatches.
- C remains rarely accepted: only confirmed success is REQ-2408, a Regional Ops small north shipment on a second attempt. Do not infer C from region, size, or prior attempts.
- B has no confirmed successes and was rejected in tested large cases, including Field Sales large east invoice. “Large = priority desk” remains unsupported.
- D is not broadly valid, including for Partner Accounts. Confirmed successes are Partner Accounts small east invoice (REQ-2423) and large north claim (REQ-2429). It was rejected for Partner Accounts small east shipment, small north refund, small south shipment/invoice, large east invoice, and large north shipment (REQ-2458).
- Prefer the closest confirmed department + request-type match. Treat urgency, “regional office,” scanned paperwork, and repeat attempts as non-determinative. Verify available options and expect exceptions within departments.
